If he does, friendly Rohan models within 6" of Háma may re-roll To Wound Rolls of a natural 1 when making Strikes until the end of the turn.

book: Armies of the Lord of the Rings
content: Race MAN Faction ROHAN Base size 25MM Unit Type HERO, INFANTRY, UNIQUE 3 2 3 Mv Fv Sv S D A W C I 6" 5 3+ 4 5 2 2 4+ 4+ The daughter of Helm and younger sister to Haleth and Háma, Héra is a wild and headstrong young woman who learned to ride a horse before she could walk. Héra has no interest in settling down, preferring to seek a life of adventure and excitement. When Edoras is attacked, Héra protects the people against the invasion of Wulf’s army. It is through the quick thinking and courage of Héra that those who could not fight were able to escape the city and reach the sanctuary of the Hornburg. HÉRA, DAUGHTER OF HELM ...............................................................70 POINTS WARGEAR Armour, hand weapons and Spyglass. Spyglass ACTIVE – Héra may ignore the Stalk Unseen special rule of enemy models, and may therefore draw Line of Sight to them as normal. HEROIC ACTIONS Heroic Defence Heroic Resolve Heroic Strike OPTIONS Ashere ..............................................................................20 points ASHERE Ashere – Ashere is a Mount that uses the profile below: SPECIAL RULES Expert Rider, Horse Lord Daughter of Rohan PASSIVE – Héra is fiercely independent and a capable warrior on her own; those that underestimate her find out the hard way that she is more than she seems. If Héra is involved in a Combat where there is only a single model on each side, and neither model is Supported, then Héra increases her Attacks characteristic to 3 and may re-roll To Wound Rolls of a natural 1 when making Strikes. Base size 40MM Unit Type MOUNT Faction ROHAN Race HORSE Mv Fv Sv S D A W C I 10" 2 6+ 3 4 0 1 7+ 7+ SPECIAL RULES Swift Gallop ACTIVE – When Héra Activates whilst mounted on Ashere, she can declare that Ashere will use this special rule. If she does, Ashere increases her Move Value to 12" and gains the Woodland Creature special rule until the end of Hera’s Activation; however, Héra cannot Charge during this Move.

book: Armies of the Lord of the Rings
content: Base size 25MM Race MAN Faction ROHAN Unit Type HERO, INFANTRY, UNIQUE 2 2 3 Mv Fv Sv S D A W C I 6" 5 4+ 4 5 3 2 5+ 5+ The Shieldmaidens of Rohan were proud warrior women of Rohan who defended their lands against invaders throughout the kingdom’s history. Though they are thought to be all but gone by the time of Helm Hammerhand’s rule, Olwyn still upholds the values and training she gained in her youth. An exceptional warrior by any standard, Olwyn will fight valiantly to protect those she is close to, in particular Héra who she imparts her wisdom onto along with the ways of the Shieldmaidens of old. OLWYN, SHIELDMAIDEN OF ROHAN...............................................80 POINTS WARGEAR Light armour, shield and hand weapon. HEROIC ACTIONS Heroic Defence Heroic Resolve OPTIONS Horse ...............................................................................20 points SPECIAL RULES Expert Rider, Horse Lord, Sworn Protector (Héra) Stalwart Fighter ACTIVE – Olwyn has been a Shieldmaiden for many years and knows how best to protect herself in battle. Whilst Olwyn is outnumbered in a Combat, enemy models will require a 6 To Wound her when making Strikes, regardless of their Strength characteristic. Note, as this does not require a natural 6, enemy models may use Might to influence their To Wound Rolls against Olwyn and any bonuses To Wound will still apply as normal.

book: Armies of the Lord of the Rings
content: Faction ROHAN Race MAN 1 5 1 Mv Fv Sv S D A W C I 6" 3 4+ 3 4 1 2 7+ 7+ Base size 25MM Unit Type HERO, INFANTRY, UNIQUE The young esquire to the king, Lief acts as Helm’s personal attendant within his court. Unlike many of his kin, Lief is not a strong rider nor particularly adept with a blade. Yet where the young esquire excels is in his loyalty to his king and the duties entrusted to him. He is often tasked with delivering the king’s decrees and scrolls containing orders to the various lords of Rohan. When Edoras comes under siege, Lief helps lead those who cannot fight away from the city and towards the Hornburg, and it is here where Lief helps Héra rally her troops to defend the Hornburg against the hordes of Hill Tribesmen outside the gates. LIEF, PAGE OF HELM..............................................................................50 POINTS WARGEAR Light armour and hand weapon. HEROIC ACTIONS Heroic Defence OPTIONS Horse ................................................................................20 points SPECIAL RULES Horse Lord Orders from Edoras PASSIVE – As the king’s attendant, it is Lief’s duty to carry around the orders of the royal line of Rohan and deliver orders to Rohan’s warriors and nobles. Lief may spend a Will Point at the end of his Activation to use this ability, so long as he is not Engaged in Combat. If he does, pick one of the following orders; its effects will last until the end of the turn. Each order can only be chosen once per game. Friendly Rohan Hero models within 3" of Lief may declare a Heroic Combat for free. Friendly Rohan models within 3" of Lief gain the Fearless special rule. Friendly Rohan models within 3" of Lief do not suffer the -1 penalty To Hit when moving and shooting and may re-roll failed To Hit Rolls when making shooting attacks. Friendly Rohan models that start their Activation within 3" of Lief gain the Woodland Creature and Mountain Dweller special rules. Friendly Rohan models that start their Activation within 3" of Lief increase their Move Value by 2".

book: Armies of the Lord of the Rings
content: Base size 25MM Race MAN Faction ROHAN Unit Type HERO, INFANTRY, UNIQUE 2 3 3 Mv Fv Sv S D A W C I 6" 6 4+ 4 5 3 3 4+ 4+ FRÉALÁF, FIRST MARSHAL OF THE RIDDERMARK......................100 POINTS The nephew of Helm Hammerhand, Fréaláf is the First Marshal of the Riddermark and the Lord of Harrowdale. Though relatively young, Fréaláf is wise beyond his years as both a warrior and a leader. When Helm Hammerhand is determined to fight Freca, it is Fréaláf who tries to convince him to stay his hand; and when the armies of Wulf surround Edoras, it is Fréaláf who urges his liege to abandon the city and get his people to safety – an act that sees him dismissed from Helm’s war room with his uncle, the king scornfully bidding him to run and hide in the stronghold of Dunharrow. Regardless, Fréaláf remains loyal to his liege and his bloodline and will ride to the aid of Héra in her most dire time of need. WARGEAR Armour and hand weapon. HEROIC ACTIONS Heroic Defence Heroic Resolve OPTIONS Horse ........................................................20 points SPECIAL RULES Expert Rider, Horse Lord Mutual Respect ACTIVE – Fréaláf holds a great deal of respect for his cousin, Héra, and will go to great lengths to protect her from any trouble she gets herself into. Whilst within 6" of Héra, Fréaláf gains the Master of Battle (4+) special rule. Lord of Harrowdale PASSIVE – The garrison from Harrowdale have a great respect for Fréaláf, and will stand by him wherever he rides. Any Warriors of Rohan included in Fréaláf’s Warband are automatically upgraded to Warriors of Harrowdale. Warriors of Harrowdale that can draw Line of Sight to Fréaláf may re-roll any failed Intelligence Tests and gain the Shieldwall special rule.

book: Armies of the Lord of the Rings
content: Base size 25MM Race MAN Faction ROHAN Unit Type HERO, INFANTRY, UNIQUE 3 3 1 Mv Fv Sv S D A W C I 6" 7 5+ 6 5 3 3 3+ 5+ Following the loss of his sons and his kingdom, and being besieged within the Hornburg, Helm Hammerhand’s grief causes him to retreat into his own mind, becoming a shadow of his former self. Yet something causes Helm to leave the fortress and traverse the snowy landscapes around the Hornburg, hunting down and slaughtering any of Wulf’s followers that he comes across with sheer brutality. Such is the rage that Helm feels towards Wulf and his armies, that he will stop at nothing to enact his revenge on every last one of them for the grief they have brought upon him and Rohan. HELM HAMMERHAND, WRAITH OF THE HORNBURG ................180 POINTS WARGEAR Light armour and Horn of the Hammerhand. Horn of the Hammerhand ACTIVE – This is a Unique war horn. Additionally, once per game at the start of any Move Phase, Helm can unleash a fearsome blow of the Horn of the Hammerhand. Until the End Phase of the turn, enemy models within 24" of Helm suffer a -1 penalty to any Courage Test they are required to make. HEROIC ACTIONS Heroic Challenge Heroic Strength Heroic Strike SPECIAL RULES Burly, Dominant (4), Fearless, Hatred (Dunland), Mighty Blow The Hammerhand ACTIVE – Helm is incredibly strong, stronger by far than normal Men, being a descendant of the great heroes of the Edain. It was said that a single punch from the King of Rohan could slay a man. Helm is never considered to be Unarmed; ever. No Longer a Leader ACTIVE – Having lost his kingdom and his sons, Helm descends into madness leaving him incapable of ruling his people. If your Army includes Helm, then he can never be your Army’s General even if he is the Hero with the highest Heroic Tier. Additionally, Helm can never call Stand Fast and friendly models cannot benefit from any Heroic Action declared by Helm. Berserk Rage ACTIVE – Driven mad by fury and grief, Helm will show no mercy to his foes and the sight of this once great king rampaging through enemy lines is a truly terrifying one. Helm Hammerhand must always Charge if he is able to do so. Additionally, if Helm Charges into Combat then he gains the Terror special rule until the End Phase of the turn, and may declare a Heroic Combat in the Fight Phase without spending Might.

book: Armies of the Lord of the Rings
content: Race MAN Base size 25MM Faction ROHAN Unit Type HERO, INFANTRY, UNIQUE 3 3 3 Mv Fv Sv S D A W C I 6" 6 3+ 4 5 3 3 4+ 4+ With her father driven mad by grief, gone missing, and her brothers both slain, Héra fulfils her duty as the last of the bloodline of Helm and leads her people in the final defence of the Hornburg. With Wulf’s army outside the gate, Héra dons the ancient wedding dress found within the bowels of the Hornburg and strides out onto the causeway in a deliberate ploy to taunt Wulf and keep his attention fixed on her. The battle that ensues proves to be Héra’s defining moment and the acts of the Bride of Death will become worthy of tales and songs of their own. HÉRA, THE BRIDE OF DEATH .............................................................125 POINTS WARGEAR Armour and hand weapon. HEROIC ACTIONS Heroic Challenge Heroic Defence Heroic Strike OPTIONS Shield ................................................................................5 points SPECIAL RULES Fearless, Unyielding Combat Stance The Warrior Bride PASSIVE – The sight of Héra in the ghostly wedding dress is an unnerving and unnatural sight, one that can make even the most confident warriors pause for thought. Enemy models Engaged in Combat with Héra cannot declare a Heroic Strike. Fury of the Hammerhand ACTIVE – As the last descendant of Helm Hammerhand, Héra fights to ensure that her bloodline is remembered for its bravery and strength. In a turn in which Héra Charges, she must re-roll any failed To Wound Rolls when making Strikes.

book: Armies of the Lord of the Rings
content: Race MAN Faction ROHAN The Rohirrim are a hardy people, having defended their lands from the forces of Evil for many years. Though Rohan does not have a standing army in the same manner as that of Gondor, those who live in the various villages and settlements still possess enough martial skill to take up arms should the need arise. Though they live in constant fear of Sauron’s shadow, and in more recent years the threat of Isengard has become a reality, the Rohirrim choose to fight this threat head-on with spear, sword and bow. Base size 25MM Race MAN Faction ROHAN Unit Type WARRIOR, INFANTRY Mv Fv Sv S D A W C I 6" 3 4+ 3 4 1 1 7+ 6+ WARRIOR OF ROHAN .....................6 POINTS Base size 25MM Unit Type HERO, INFANTRY 2 1 1 Mv Fv Sv S D A W C I 6" 4 4+ 4 5 2 2 6+ 6+ Those who captain bands of Rohan’s armies come from many walks of life. Whether village herdsmen, or the noble lords of greater settlements, these captains all share the same traits – a great skill from horseback, wisdom and patience on the battlefield, and the loyalty of those they lead. When marauding bands of Wild Men of Dunland, Orcs or Uruk-hai assault the lands of Rohan, these captains will lead their warriors in defence of the kingdom without hesitation. CAPTAIN OF ROHAN .....................45 POINTS WARGEAR Armour and hand weapon. HEROIC ACTIONS Heroic March OPTIONS Horse .......................................................................................................20 points Exchange armour for heavy armour....................................................5 points Shield .........................................................................................................5 points SPECIAL RULES Expert Rider, Horse Lord WARGEAR Armour and hand weapon. OPTIONS A Warrior of Rohan must have one of the following options for the listed points cost: War horn, shield and throwing spears.............................................28 points Banner.....................................................................................................25 points Shield and throwing spears...................................................................3 points Bow...............................................................................................................1 point Shield ...........................................................................................................1 point SPECIAL RULES Spear Mastery ACTIVE – Throwing spears are a common weapon in Rohan and the Rohirrim have become adept at using them both up close and from afar. This model may use its throwing spears as a normal spear during the Fight Phase, so long as it hasn’t made a shooting attack with it in either the preceding Move Phase or Shoot Phase.

book: Armies of the Lord of the Rings
content: Race MAN Race MAN Faction ROHAN Faction ROHAN Base size 25MM Unit Type WARRIOR, INFANTRY, ELITE The most skilled warriors in Rohan are drafted into the royal guard and given the duty of protecting the king and the royal line of Rohan. Handpicked for their skill-at-arms, the Rohan Royal Guard spend their time further honing their skill with a blade to ensure that they can match any foe who threatens their liege. These warriors form the spearhead of Rohan’s armies, fighting without fear at the side of their king, their polished mail and pointed spears glinting in the sun. ROHAN ROYAL GUARD ..................11 POINTS Mv Fv Sv S D A W C I 6" 4 4+ 3 6 1 1 7+ 6+ Base size 25MM Unit Type WARRIOR, CAVALRY The pride of Rohan’s armies are her riders. It has long been said that the skill of the horse lords of Rohan are without rival amongst the riders of Men, and there are some who claim that they can even match that of the Elves. Regardless, their skill from horseback is undeniable, born out of generations of training, wisdom and experience. Many a general has been on the receiving end of a devastating Rohirrim charge, only to find their forces scattered and cut down. Mv Fv Sv S D A W C I 6" 3 4+ 3 5 1 1 7+ 6+ RIDER OF ROHAN ..........................14 POINTS WARGEAR Armour, shield, hand weapon, bow and horse. OPTIONS A Rider of Rohan may have one of the following options for the listed points cost: Banner.....................................................................................................25 points Throwing spears ......................................................................................2 points SPECIAL RULES Expert Rider Spear Mastery ACTIVE – See page 46. Arise, Riders of Rohan! ACTIVE – When inspired to fight, the Riders of Rohan will charge forth into the fray for the glory of Rohan and its people. If this model is within 12" of a Rohan General and has the Cavalry keyword, then it gains a bonus of +1 to its Fight Value in a turn in which it Charges. WARGEAR Heavy armour, shield and hand weapon. OPTIONS A Rohan Royal Guard may have one of the following options for the listed points cost: Horse and throwing spears ...................................................................7 points Horse ..........................................................................................................5 points Throwing spears ......................................................................................2 points SPECIAL RULES Bodyguard, Expert Rider Spear Mastery ACTIVE – See page 46. Arise Riders of Rohan! ACTIVE – See above.

book: Armies of the Lord of the Rings
content: Race MAN Base size 25MM Faction GONDOR Unit Type HERO, INFANTRY, UNIQUE 3 3 3 Mv Fv Sv S D A W C I 6" 7 3+ 4 7 3 3 4+ 3+ Although he is the heir of Elendil and the rightful King of Gondor, Aragorn turned from that path long ago, instead choosing to live the life of a ranger and roam the wilderness of Middle-earth. Yet at the Battle of Pelennor Fields Aragorn finally returned to Minas Tirith, bringing with him an army that turned the tide of battle. Following his victory, Aragorn has finally taken up his birthright as king and rallied his allies to march upon the Black Gate to draw out Sauron’s forces, and buy Frodo some much needed time to cross Mordor unimpeded. The coming of King Elessar heralds not only the downfall of the Dark Lord but also a change in the fortunes of the free peoples of Middle-earth. ARAGORN, KING ELESSAR.........225 POINTS WARGEAR Heavy armour, the Ring of Barahir and Andúril, Flame of the West. Ring of Barahir PASSIVE – This is a Unique piece of Wargear. Whenever Aragorn is affected by a Magical Power, after any Resist Tests have been made (if able), he may roll a D6. On a natural 6, Aragorn is not affected by that Magical Power. Andúril, Flame of the West ACTIVE – This is a Unique Elven hand-and-a- half weapon. Whenever Aragorn makes Strikes with Andúril, he never requires more than a 4+ when rolling To Wound. If Aragorn uses Andúril as a two-handed weapon, then he will still gain the bonus of +1 when rolling To Wound, meaning he will Wound on a 3+. HEROIC ACTIONS Heroic Challenge Heroic Defence Heroic March Heroic Resolve Heroic Strength Heroic Strike OPTIONS Armoured horse....................................................................................25 points SPECIAL RULES Horse Lord, Mighty Hero, Resistant to Magic “Stand, Men of the West” PASSIVE – Aragorn is able to inspire even the most humble of warriors to great deeds of valour in the face of evil. Friendly models treat Aragorn, King Elessar as a banner with a range of 6".

book: Armies of the Lord of the Rings
content: Base size 25MM Faction GONDOR Race MAN Unit Type HERO, INFANTRY, UNIQUE 2 3 1 Mv Fv Sv S D A W C I 6" 5 4+ 4 6 2 2 5+ 5+ The Steward of Gondor at the time of the War of the Ring, Denethor has ruled over Gondor for many years. Although he was once a great and valorous man, in recent years Denethor’s mind has become fragile, something made worse by the sudden loss of his beloved son, Boromir. With Minas Tirith under siege, Denethor’s mind has shattered, causing him to abandon all reason and opting to join the heathen kings of old – setting himself alight atop a funeral pyre. DENETHOR, STEWARD OF GONDOR ..........................................50 POINTS WARGEAR Heavy armour and hand weapon. HEROIC ACTIONS Heroic Defence SPECIAL RULES Leader (Citadel Guard), Leader (Guard of the Fountain Court) Broken Mind ACTIVE – The loss of Boromir has driven Denethor to madness, and there are times when he cannot recognise friend from foe. During each Priority Phase, after Priority has been determined, Denethor must take an Intelligence Test. If the test is passed, all is fine and Denethor acts as normal. If the test is failed, then during this turn Denethor is controlled by the opposing player and will be Activated during that player’s Activation Phase as if he is one of their models, and may even Charge and fight models from his own Army. When Denethor is Activated by the opposing player he is still considered to be a friendly model, and so friendly models cannot target him with shooting attacks or Magical Powers that cause damage, and may not make Strikes against him if they beat him in a Combat. When Denethor is under the control of the opposing player, they cannot use any of Denethor’s Might, Will or Fate Points. Even when under the control of the opposing player, Denethor always counts as a model in his controlling player’s Army. If Boromir is part of the same Army, then Denethor will automatically pass this Intelligence Test so long as Boromir is alive. However, should Boromir be slain, then Denethor will automatically fail the next Intelligence Test he has to make for this special rule.

book: Armies of the Lord of the Rings
content: Base size 25MM Race MAN Faction GONDOR Unit Type HERO, INFANTRY, UNIQUE 3 6 3 Mv Fv Sv S D A W C I 6" 7 4+ 4 6 3 3 4+ 5+ The boldest and most able commander that Minas Tirith has to offer, and the favoured son of Denethor, Boromir has led the armies of the White City to countless victories against the forces of the Dark Lord. When Osgiliath fell into the clutches of Mordor, it was Boromir who rallied his warriors and reclaimed the city from Orcish control. More than once has Boromir inspired his Men to great deeds of valour far above what would be expected of them, seizing a great victory from the edge of defeat. BOROMIR, CAPTAIN OF THE WHITE TOWER ..............160 POINTS WARGEAR Heavy armour, hand weapon and Horn of Gondor. Horn of Gondor ACTIVE – This is a Unique war horn. At the start of a Combat involving Boromir, if he is outnumbered in the Combat then he may blow the Horn of Gondor. If he does, then one enemy model involved in the Combat (chosen by their controlling player) must take a Courage Test. If the Courage Test is passed then the Combat is fought as normal. If the Courage Test is failed then no Duel Roll is made and Boromir automatically wins the Combat. HEROIC ACTIONS Heroic Challenge Heroic Strength Heroic Strike OPTIONS Banner of Minas Tirith.........................................................................40 points Horse .......................................................................................................20 points Shield .........................................................................................................5 points Banner of Minas Tirith PASSIVE – This is a Unique banner with a range of 6". Boromir does not suffer the -1 penalty to his Duel Roll for carrying a banner. Additionally, if a friendly Gondor Warrior model within range of the Banner of Minas Tirith is involved in a Drawn Combat, and the Combat is tied at the Gondor Warrior model’s Fight Value (i.e., both sides have Fight Value 4 as their highest), then instead of rolling off to see who wins, the Gondor Warrior model wins instead. If both sides have a similar special rule, roll off as normal. SPECIAL RULES Leader (Citadel Guard) Son of Gondor ACTIVE – Boromir is the greatest warrior within the lands of Gondor, and few can hope to match his skill with a blade or his ferocity in battle. In a turn in which he Charges, Boromir gains a bonus of +1 To Wound when making Strikes.

book: Armies of the Lord of the Rings
content: Race MAN Base size 25MM Faramir has ever lived in the shadow of his brother, at least in the eyes of his father. Yet Faramir is still a capable warrior in his own right and a veteran of many campaigns against the forces of the Dark Lord. It is Faramir who commands the Rangers of Gondor and the defence of Osgiliath following his brother’s departure for Rivendell. It was in Osgiliath where Faramir proved his true quality; for there are very few Men who can say they heard the call of the One Ring and managed to resist its temptation – not even his brother. Faction GONDOR Unit Type HERO, INFANTRY, UNIQUE 3 3 2 Mv Fv Sv S D A W C I 6" 6 3+ 4 5 3 2 4+ 4+ FARAMIR, CAPTAIN OF GONDOR .................................100 POINTS WARGEAR Armour, hand weapon and bow. HEROIC ACTIONS Heroic Accuracy Heroic Defence Heroic Resolve Heroic Strike OPTIONS Horse .......................................................................................................20 points Shield .........................................................................................................5 points Exchange armour and bow for heavy armour..........................................Free SPECIAL RULES Leader (Citadel Guard), Resistant to Magic, Sharpshooter, Woodland Creature “A Chance for Faramir, Captain of Gondor to show his Quality” ACTIVE Few can say they had the strength of will to resist the call of the Ring, and it is this very strength that Faramir can call upon in the direst of situations. Should Faramir’s Army be Broken, then from that point onwards Faramir may re-roll any failed To Wound Rolls when making Strikes. Additionally, should Faramir’s Army be Broken, then Faramir may declare a Heroic Resolve each turn for free. Wizard’s Pupil PASSIVE – Having been taught by Gandalf, Faramir is able to command his Men with patience and wisdom. Whilst Faramir is alive and on the battlefield, if you win the roll to choose who has Priority, and choose to give Priority to your opponent, then until the end of the turn Faramir and friendly Warrior models within 3" of him gain the Dominant (2) special rule.

book: Armies of the Lord of the Rings
content: Base size 25MM Race WIZARD Faction FELLOWSHIP Unit Type HERO, INFANTRY, UNIQUE 3 0 6 2 3 1 Mv Fv Sv S D A W C I 6" 6 4+ 4 6 3 3 3+ 3+ Though he fell in Moria in his duel with the Balrog, Gandalf’s story did not end there. Instead, he was sent back to Middle-earth until his task was complete, this time as the White Wizard. In his new guise, Gandalf is even more powerful than he was before, stripping Saruman of his power as Lord of the Istari. When war comes to Minas Tirith, it is Gandalf the White who leads the final defence of the city, inspiring the Men of Gondor to stand firm and hold their ground against the hordes of Mordor. GANDALF THE WHITE................200 POINTS WARGEAR Glamdring, Narya and Staff of Power. Glamdring ACTIVE – This is a Unique Elven hand-and-a-half weapon. A model gains a bonus of +1 to their Strength when making Strikes with Glamdring. Narya PASSIVE – This is a Unique piece of Wargear. Gandalf may re-roll any failed Fate rolls. HEROIC ACTIONS Heroic Channelling Heroic Defence Heroic Resolve Heroic Strike SHADOWFAX Shadowfax is a Mount that uses the profile below: OPTIONS Pippin......................................................................................................25 points (can only be taken if Gandalf is riding Shadowfax) Shadowfax .............................................................................................25 points Pippin PASSIVE – If Gandalf is upgraded to take Pippin, then Pippin will be treated as a Passenger on Shadowfax. Pippin uses the Peregrin Took, Guard of the Citadel profile (see page 54) and will always count as an Independent Hero in this instance. Pippin will still count as a model towards the Army’s total number of models and Break Point, though will not take up a space in Gandalf’s Warband. Whilst Pippin is mounted on Shadowfax, Gandalf gains the Resistant to Magic special rule, may re-roll To Wound Rolls of a natural 1 when making Strikes, and can spend Pippin’s Might, Will and Fate Points as if they were his own. book: Armies of the Lord of the Rings
content: Upon reaching the White City, Pippin pledges his service to Denethor in payment for Boromir saving his life and joins the ranks of the Citadel Guard. It is during the battle for Minas Tirith where it becomes apparent that there is little left of the impetuous Hobbit who set off from the Shire. Instead, Pippin has become a courageous and valuable ally, earning the respect of those within Minas Tirith. content: 1 2 2 Race MAN Faction GONDOR Unit Type HERO, INFANTRY, UNIQUE Base size 25MM Mv Fv Sv S D A W C I 6" 5 4+ 4 6 2 2 6+ 6+ IROLAS, CAPTAIN OF THE GUARD ...............................65 POINTS Irolas is the captain of the Citadel Guard and a loyal bodyguard to Lord Denethor. During the siege of Minas Tirith, Irolas commands those atop the walls of the White City, directing his warriors to defend the fortress against the onslaught of Orcs. Irolas is a skilled swordsman in his own right, and those who mistake his defensive stance with a blade for simply being cautious will often find themselves on the receiving end of a rush of steel. WARGEAR Heavy armour and hand weapon. HEROIC ACTIONS Heroic Defence SPECIAL RULES Leader (Citadel Guard), Sworn Protector (Denethor) Defend the White City ACTIVE – With a whirl of steel, Irolas is able to deflect incoming blows before plunging his sword into the flesh of his enemies. Irolas may use the Shielding special rule even though he is not armed with a shield. If Irolas elects to shield, and wins the ensuing Combat, he may make a single Strike against one enemy model that was involved in the Combat. Captain of the Citadel Guard PASSIVE – Irolas commands the Citadel Guard into battle, urging them on to defend the White City at all costs. Friendly Citadel Guard within 3" of Irolas gain a bonus of +1 To Wound when making Strikes.

book: Armies of the Lord of the Rings
content: Race MAN Base size 25MM Base size 25MM Unit Type HERO, INFANTRY, UNIQUE Unit Type HERO, INFANTRY, UNIQUE An experienced veteran within the ranks of Faramir’s rangers, Madril has seen many conflicts over his years in the service of the White Tower. Having long served at the side of his commander, Madril is Faramir’s most trusted captain and takes up command of Osgiliath when Faramir ventures into Ithilien. When the armies of Mordor invade Osgiliath, it is the ambushes set in place by Madril that keeps the onslaught at bay for long enough for many of Gondor’s forces to be able to escape to safety. When the armies of Mordor advance upon Osgiliath, Damrod takes up sword and bow in defence of his homeland. book: Armies of the Lord of the Rings
content: Retaking Osgiliath from the clutches of Mordor proved to be a difficult task, one entrusted to the bravest warriors Minas Tirith could spare and led by the steward’s own sons, Boromir and Faramir. Those who survived became known as Osgiliath Veterans – grizzled warriors who stopped at nothing to ensure the former capital was returned to Gondor. Though their armour is battered and their flesh is scarred, the loyalty of these veterans to their captains remains completely unscathed. Mv Fv Sv S D A W C I 6" 4 4+ 3 5 1 1 6+ 6+ Race MAN Faction GONDOR OSGILIATH VETERAN......................9 POINTS Mv Fv Sv S D A W C I 6" 4 3+ 3 4 1 1 7+ 6+ Race MAN Base size 25MM Base size 25MM Unit Type WARRIOR, INFANTRY Unit Type WARRIOR, INFANTRY Faction GONDOR RANGER OF GONDOR.....................8 POINTS The Rangers of Gondor are tasked with protecting the kingdom’s borders from intruders and the spies of the enemy, and they do not take kindly to those who trespass into Gondor. Each ranger is a skilled hunter, archer and tracker, adept at travelling almost unheard and unseen through the thick undergrowth that makes up Ithilien. Those who do attempt to sneak into Gondor will likely be faced with a flurry of arrows before they know they are being watched. WARGEAR Armour, hand weapon and bow. book: Armies of the Lord of the Rings

These captains each have many years of experience on the battlefield and have all been trained in the art of warfare by the very best commanders Minas Tirith has to offer. When the armies of Mordor threaten to raze the White City to the ground, it is the courage and steely determination of these captains that will steady those around them to fight. book: Armies of the Lord of the Rings
content: The warriors who excel in riding a horse join the ranks of the Knights of Minas Tirith, leading the charge from the head of Gondor’s armies as they gallop into the fray. The charge of the Knights of Minas Tirith is a fearsome one; their razor-sharp lances piercing both armour and flesh as they scatter enemy battlelines and leave the broken remnants of their foes’ formations in their wake. Mv Fv Sv S D A W C I 6" 4 4+ 3 6 1 1 7+ 7+ Race MAN Faction GONDOR KNIGHT OF MINAS TIRITH............15 POINTS The Men who make up the rank and file of Gondor’s forces are the backbone of her armies. Each warrior is clad in thick armour, emblazoned with the motif of the White Tree of Gondor, and armed with expertly crafted swords, shields or spears. On the battlefield, the warriors of Minas Tirith fight in disciplined battle formations designed to outclass their enemies and protect their allies. These Men have fought many battles against the armies of Mordor, all in the name of keeping the rest of Middle-earth safe from Sauron’s influence. Mv Fv Sv S D A W C I 6" 4 4+ 3 5 1 1 7+ 7+ WARRIOR OF MINAS TIRITH .........8 POINTS Race MAN Base size 25MM Base size 25MM Unit Type WARRIOR, CAVALRY Unit Type WARRIOR, INFANTRY Faction GONDOR WARGEAR Heavy armour and hand weapon. book: Armies of the Lord of the Rings
content: The most disciplined warriors in Minas Tirith are selected to join the Guard of the Fountain Court, swearing their lives to serve the White City no matter the peril the city finds itself in. Stalwart and proud, these warriors truly are the pinnacle of Minas Tirith’s armies. Although they are too few in number to form whole regiments, these stoic warriors serve as bodyguards to the nobles and leaders of the White City. content: Base size 25MM Race MAN Unit Type HERO, INFANTRY, UNIQUE Faction NÚMENOR 3 3 1 Mv Fv Sv S D A W C I 6" 8 4+ 5 7 3 3 4+ 4+ Arguably the greatest Man in the history of Middle-earth, it was Elendil who led the Men of Númenor to Eriador following the drowning of their island homeland, and he who founded the kingdoms of Gondor and Arnor. A wise and noble king, Elendil was unmatched in combat within the race of Men. When the Dark Lord threatened to plunge Middle-earth into darkness, Elendil and his sons led their people against the forces of Mordor and fought for the future of Middle-earth on the slopes of Mount Doom. Though he was tragically slain by Sauron, Elendil’s sacrifice ultimately sealed the fate of Middle-earth, protecting the free lands from the Dark Lord’s tyranny. ELENDIL, HIGH KING OF GONDOR AND ARNOR...........175 POINTS WARGEAR Heavy armour and Narsil. Narsil ACTIVE – This is a Unique Master-forged two-handed weapon. The range of Elendil’s Stand Fast is 12" rather than 6".

Yet upon Isildur taking the One Ring, the spirit of Sauron was able to latch onto him, corrupting the prince into keeping the Ring instead of destroying it. Though he kept it to be an heirloom of his kingdom, the Ring ended up betraying Isildur to his death, and the Ring was lost in the waters of the Anduin, allowing the will of Sauron to endure. ISILDUR, PRINCE OF NÚMENOR.....130 POINTS WARGEAR Heavy armour and hand-and-a-half weapon. If your Army also contains Elendil, then if Elendil is slain, place a 25mm Marker where he was killed. If Isildur ends his Activation within 1" of this Marker, he may gain the Shards of Narsil – remove the Marker. The Shards of Narsil are a Unique hand weapon, and a model fighting with it in Combat gains a bonus of +1 To Wound when making Strikes.

book: Armies of the Lord of the Rings

Stronger than the Men of later ages, clad in sable-coloured robes and armed with the best steel-forged swords of the age, these courageous warriors marched upon Mordor and Mount Doom in a final bid to bring down the Dark Lord. content: Base size 25MM Race SPIRIT Faction DUNHARROW Unit Type HERO, INFANTRY, UNIQUE 1 6 3 Mv Fv Sv S D A W C I 8" 6 4+ 4 8 2 3 3+ 5+ KING OF THE DEAD ....................100 POINTS When the armies of Númenor were preparing to go to war with Sauron, the king of the mountains swore an oath to Isildur that he and his people would join their fight; yet when the time came, they refused, resulting in Isildur cursing them to not rest until their oath is fulfilled. Though his body has long been reduced to dust, the king’s spirit lingers on in torment until he honours his word. It is the coming of Aragorn that has finally provided the opportunity, and the King of the Dead has pledged to join the heir of Isildur and take up arms against the armies of Mordor – the oath sworn to Isildur will finally be fulfilled and the dead will be able to rest in peace. WARGEAR Armour and hand weapon. HEROIC ACTIONS Heroic March Heroic Strike SPECIAL RULES Blades of the Dead, Spectral Walk, Terror Drain Soul ACTIVE – The dread powers harnessed by the King of the Dead are powerful enough to drain the essence of his victims. A model that suffers a Wound from the King of the Dead in Combat, which is not then prevented, will automatically have their Wounds reduced to 0, causing them to be slain and removed as a casualty. The Dead and the Living PASSIVE – The King of the Dead has no power over the living and can only command those under the effects of the same curse as himself. Only friendly Dunharrow models may benefit from the King of the Dead’s Stand Fast or benefit from his Heroic Actions.

book: Armies of the Lord of the Rings
content: Base size 25MM Unit Type WARRIOR, INFANTRY Faction DUNHARROW Race SPIRIT Those who broke the oath sworn to Isildur suffered a terrible curse, forcing them to linger on. Over the centuries of the Third Age, their bodies began to decay and slowly turn to dust; yet they did not rest. Instead they became spectral shadows of their former selves, forced to wander their mountain homes in shame. A grim fate awaits any who stray into the realm of the dead. Though their blades have long since lost their edge, the armour of mortal beings holds no defence against them, cutting through their very soul. WARRIOR OF THE DEAD ..............14 POINTS Mv Fv Sv S D A W C I 8" 3 4+ 3 7 1 1 4+ 6+ Base size 25MM These proud warriors once held their king’s colours aloft in life and gave counsel to their liege in times of war and conflict. Even in death they continue to fulfil their purpose; though their bodies are reduced to naught but a spectral shell and their once proud pennants are tattered and torn, these heralds still fight at the side of their king, determined to honour the position they once held in life. Riding out ahead of their allies upon ghastly steeds, these dread apparitions are enough to chill the souls of their enemies and cause utter panic within the ranks of those who they charge. Much like their counterparts on foot, the weapons of these ghostly riders are spectral in nature, and care not for plate or mail as they find their mark. It was Gil-galad who forged the Last Alliance with Elendil, marching upon Mordor for the freedom of Middle-earth. Such was Gil-galad’s bravery that he stood toe-to-toe with the Dark Lord himself, wielding his great Elven spear, Aiglos. Though he would not live to see the Dark Lord defeated, for he perished at Sauron’s hands, the name of Gil-galad lived on in songs and legend, honouring the great sacrifice of the Elven king. book: Armies of the Lord of the Rings
content: THE FELLOWSHIP I n all the long history of Middle-earth, there are few heroes as celebrated and admired as the legendary Fellowship of the Ring. Formed at the Council of Elrond in Rivendell, this unlikely band of nine companions pledged to do the impossible – to journey to the depths of Mordor and cast the One Ring into the fires of Mount Doom, destroying it and freeing Middle-earth from the darkness of Sauron. Led by the wandering Istari, Gandalf the Grey, the Fellowship contained representatives from all the races of the free peoples. From the race of Men, a ranger of the north going by the name of Strider, and the noble Boromir from the city of Minas Tirith. From the Dwarves, the stubborn and steadfast Gimli, son of Glóin, a formidable warrior in his own right. And from the Elves, Legolas Greenleaf of the woodland realm, who would ensure that the Elves would finally see the power of the Ring ended, as it should have been over 3,000 years before. THE FELLOWSHIP However, most importantly, the Fellowship contained four Hobbits – the most unlikely creatures to join such an epic quest. Frodo Baggins, joined by Samwise Gamgee, Meriadoc Brandybuck and Peregrin Took, set out to deliver the One Ring to Rivendell, only to be thrust into an adventure beyond their wildest imaginations. For the Hobbits who had never left the borders of the Shire, the journey would be filled with perils they’d never encountered before, and would take every ounce of courage they could muster to succeed. The journey to Mordor would prove to be one fraught with danger, and everywhere the servants of the enemy would seek to track down and slay the Fellowship in a bid to reclaim the One Ring for their dark master. Yet hope would endure so long as the Fellowship stayed true to each other; though they would each be pushed to their limits on every step of their journey, and not all of them would live to see the end of their tale…

book: Armies of the Lord of the Rings
content: THE SHIRE T he Hobbits of the Shire are a peaceful race, quite content to ignore, and be ignored by, the comings and goings of the world outside their borders. In fact, many in Middle-earth are oblivious to the existence of Hobbits entirely, and those that are aware of Hobbits see them as of little or no relevance at all. Not that this troubles the Hobbits in the slightest, and they are quite happy to just go about their simple life without being bothered by the ‘big-folk’. On the whole, the Hobbits of the Shire live a quaint, idyllic lifestyle away from the hustle and bustle of towns and cities, enjoying the simple things life offers such as sampling good food, the brewing of ales and the smoking of pipe-weed. However, where their hearts truly lie is in peace and quiet and good tilled earth, for all Hobbits share a love of things that grow – and it is for these reasons that a Hobbit makes for an excellent gardener. THE SHIRE Yet if there is one thing Hobbits enjoy even more than peace and quiet, it’s a good party filled with merriment, laughter and, of course, fireworks. Perhaps the most notable of such events was the 111th birthday of one Mr Bilbo Baggins; half the Shire was said to be invited, and the other half seemingly turned up anyway. Even Bilbo’s disgruntled relatives, the Sackville-Baggins, made an appearance, Lobelia proving to be particularly unpleasant as she ranted the ear off of Bilbo. The fireworks were provided by the wandering Wizard, Gandalf the Grey. Gandalf has long been an ally of the Shire, having visited its rolling green hills many times over the years, and became known for aiding them in times of need. However, in more recent times Gandalf has been labelled as a disturber of the peace, possibly in relation to his part in Bilbo’s adventures with the Dragon, and him coming back far more ‘odd’ than when he left. Regardless, Gandalf will still come to the Shire should the Hobbits ever be in true need.

content: ROAD TO RIVENDELL ROAD TO RIVENDELL H aving been gifted the One Ring by his uncle, Frodo has been tasked by Gandalf to deliver it to Rivendell and the safety of the Elves. To accompany him on this journey, Frodo brings with him some of his most trusted friends from the Shire: Samwise Gamgee, Meriadoc Brandybuck and Peregrin Took. Though they may not be initially aware of the dangers that will face them, the Hobbits will bravely stand by Frodo against any who threaten him. Upon the Hobbits’ arrival in Bree, they make for the inn of the Prancing Pony, allowed entry to the town during the pouring rain and under the cover of darkness by the Gatekeeper of Bree. It is within the Prancing Pony where Frodo and his companions are able to enjoy their first good meal, large pints and warm hearth since they set out from the Shire, all of which are catered for them by the jolly innkeeper, Barliman Butterbur; who also manages to secure them a pony by the name of Bill. Yet it is not just Barliman the Hobbits encounter in Bree. Within the shadows of the Prancing Pony a mysterious man is watching the Hobbits closely who, upon Frodo’s mishap and accidental slipping on of the Ring, reveals himself to be Strider, an ally of Gandalf. This Strider seems to know about the nature of the Ring and the terrifying Black Riders that hunt them, and offers to help Frodo and his companions to evade the clutches of the Nazgûl, guiding them through the wilderness and onwards to Rivendell. Yet even Strider can not keep the Nazgûl off their trail entirely, and they eventually catch up to the Hobbits at Weathertop, resulting in Frodo being stabbed with a Morgul Blade. After driving the Nazgûl off, Strider attempts to slow the poison, only to be caught off-guard by the Elf-maid, Arwen. Knowing that the only chance for Frodo to survive is for him to reach Rivendell and the medicine her father can provide, Arwen rides with Frodo as fast as she can, though she will need to ride as swift as the wind if she is to outride the Nazgûl…

book: Armies of the Lord of the Rings
content: BREAKING OF THE FELLOWSHIP I t is within the sanctuary of Lothlórien that the Fellowship came for refuge following their ordeals in Moria, for the loss of Gandalf in the chasms of the fallen Dwarven kingdom had left the Fellowship devoid of direction and in need of guidance in their quest. Upon reaching the borders of Lothlórien, the Fellowship is halted by Haldir who has to be convinced by Aragorn to take them to Caras Galadhon and before the Lady Galadriel. Guided by Haldir, the Fellowship makes their way through the woodland realm and to the great tree-city of Caras Galadhon. Upon their arrival, Galadriel and Celeborn greet the members of the Fellowship, offering them the chance to rest and regather their strength for the journey ahead; and before the Fellowship set out again they are clad in the garb of Lothlórien, which is usually reserved for the Galadhrim and no others, and each presented with a gift from Galadriel. BREAKING OF THE FELLOWSHIP The gifts bestowed unto the Fellowship are individual, personal items that will have significance only to those they are given to. Though they may not know it, each gift will prove useful to the Fellowship as they continue on their quest to save Middle-earth. Some gain weaponry to help them fight off the perils that lie ahead, whilst others are given items that at first glance may seem less useful, but in fact will be integral to the success of the Fellowship. Setting out from the safety of Lothlórien and the protection of the Lady Galadriel, the Fellowship knows that their toughest days are still in front of them. Yet the gifts they have each been presented with also come with a renewed sense of hope; hope that they may yet succeed in their heroic quest, and hope that together they can finally bring about the destruction of the One Ring and save Middle-earth from darkness.

book: Armies of the Lord of the Rings
content: KINGDOM OF ROHAN B efore the Wizard Saruman poisoned Théoden’s mind, the kingdom of Rohan had flourished under its king’s rule. Yet even then, Rohan found itself constantly needing to defend its borders against bands of Orcs and Wild Men of Dunland who sought to bring ruin upon them. The sons of Rohan are forced to become warriors and wield a blade far sooner than those of other races out of necessity. Whilst Théoden rules from the city of Edoras, his armies are led by his royal bloodline and his most trusted marshals and captains. The king’s own son, Théodred, commands Rohan’s forces in battle, leading Éoreds of Riders of Rohan against their enemies. The prince is a fierce and capable warrior who has fought many battles in his short life, though his victories have instilled a great sense of pride in Théodred, one that can manifest as arrogance and may yet become the prince’s downfall. KINGDOM OF ROHAN Beneath the Prince of Rohan are the Marshals of the Riddermark, the foremost of Rohan’s warriors, with each of them harbouring a great amount of battlefield experience and skill at arms. Perhaps the greatest of these is Éomer, the nephew of Théoden. An exceptional warrior and rider even by the standards of the Rohirrim, Éomer is unshakably loyal to his liege and will fight with all his might to protect the lands he has sworn his life to serve. The pride of Rohan’s armies are undoubtedly her riders, which are the envy of the races of Men across Middle-earth. Few can boast the sheer levels of skill that the Riders of Rohan can bring, with each one being an expert combatant from horseback. Led by their captains, the Rohirrim will face any enemy that threatens their lands head-on, forging their own stories of daring and heroism that will rival even those of their forebears and the heroic deeds they achieved during the great history of Rohan.

Armies of the Lord of the Rings
content: ROAD TO HELM’S DEEP ROAD TO HELM’S DEEP H is mind now freed from the clutches of Saruman, Théoden is made aware of all that has befallen his kingdom. Not only has he lost his only son, Théodred, but Rohan finds itself weakened and Edoras vulnerable to attack. Knowing that Saruman will not relinquish his hold on Rohan lightly, Gandalf advises Théoden to lead his people to the refuge of Helm’s Deep in order to weather the inevitable assault from the armies of Isengard. Seeing there to be no other option if his people are to survive, Théoden orders Edoras to be evacuated and its people to begin the trek to Helm’s Deep. Any able men are tasked with protecting the convoy, riding ahead to scout out the path or holding back to ensure none of Saruman’s spies are following. Though Gandalf has gone to look for aid elsewhere, the Rohirrim are joined by Aragorn, Legolas and Gimli, all of whom pledge to protect the people they now ride with. Yet the road to Helm’s Deep is a long and dangerous one. The convoy is slow and ponderous, containing many women, children and livestock as they trudge towards Helm’s Deep. It is this that makes the Rohirrim an easy target for attack – one which Saruman foresees. In a bid to slay the people of Rohan and to take control of the kingdom, Saruman commands his packs of Warg Riders to attack them on the road. With their enemies bearing down upon them, Théoden leads his most capable warriors to meet them head-on – ensuring they are fighting away from the people he is aiming to protect. Armed with sword, spears and a steely determination, the riders under Théoden’s command crash into their enemies, using the full force of their cavalry charge to inflict great damage upon their foes – their sole aim to buy the people of Rohan enough time to reach the safety of Helm’s Deep.

book: Armies of the Lord of the Rings
content: DEFENDERS OF HELM’S DEEP DEFENDERS OF HELM’S DEEP T he assault upon the Westfold has forced the people of Rohan to flee to the sanctuary of Helm’s Deep; the attack on their lands having highlighted their need for greater protection and taller walls. Having journeyed across Rohan and survived the ambush of the Wolves of Isengard, the Rohirrim have reached Helm’s Deep and begin to prepare for the inevitable battle against the armies of the White Hand. Whilst Théoden prepares his people for the seemingly hopeless battle that now faces them, the sound of horns calls out across the vale. Yet this is no Orc horn, and the sound signals the arrival of Haldir and an army of Elves from Lothlórien. Théoden and Aragorn welcome Haldir and his kin into the fortress and with their arrival hope is rekindled; perhaps the combined might of Men and Elves could triumph once more. As the legions of Saruman’s fighting Uruk-hai come into view, the heavens open and unleash a downpour upon the fortress of Helm’s Deep. Théoden stands atop the Hornburg with his trusted guard, ready to command his forces in the coming battle. Upon the Deeping Wall, ranks of Men and Elves stand side-by-side with one another, honouring the allegiance that stood between Elendil and Gil-galad over three thousand years ago. Those that defend Helm’s Deep are some of the greatest warriors of the Third Age. Aragorn, Legolas and Gimli stand upon the Deeping Wall and, along with Haldir, lead those atop the fortress walls against the Uruk-hai below. Though it will take every ounce of skill and martial prowess for them to overcome the seemingly impossible odds that now face them, Helm’s Deep may once again prove to be Rohan’s salvation.

book: Armies of the Lord of the Rings
content: RIDE OUT W ith the Uruk-hai having stormed over the battlements of Helm’s Deep and slaughtered many of those who had strived to defend it, it seems as though victory is within the grasp of the armies of the White Hand. Those who still survive have fallen back to the keep, barring themselves within the throne room. A sense of hopelessness and despair has begun to seep into the minds of the survivors, and even King Théoden believes that their time has now come. Yet Aragorn is not ready to give up the fight. Stirring Théoden with a moving speech of how the Rohirrim and their allies have fought and died to defend Helm’s Deep, Aragorn convinces the king to ride out one last time against the Uruk- hai that are attempting to break down the doors. Gathering their horses, Théoden and his allies prepare for one final charge in a bid to rout the fighting Uruk-hai – a charge that will result in either death or glory. RIDE OUT When the time is right, Gimli lets out a great blast on the Horn of the Hammerhand that echoes around the valley, signalling Théoden’s charge out from the doors of his keep. Aragorn and Legolas ride alongside Théoden, felling enemies from horseback with both blade and bow, giving their all to deliver Helm’s Deep from the onslaught of Isengard. The king’s Royal Guard are led by Gamling, who himself carries the Royal Standard of Rohan aloft. Should this be the last stand of the Rohirrim, then Gamling will ensure that the king’s colours fly for as long as possible. Those who ride out alongside Théoden know that hope is all but lost, and this will likely prove to be their doom; yet they do so anyway in a final attempt to fight for freedom and break the Uruk-hai that have them besieged. For it is when the darkness is greatest that hope shines the most brightly, and so long as Helm’s Deep still has warriors willing to fight to defend it, then it shall not fall.

book: Armies of the Lord of the Rings
content: RIDERS OF ÉOMER T he siege of Helm’s Deep is well underway and things are looking bleak for the armies of Rohan. The Deeping Wall has been breached, a section reduced to rubble in an explosion of fire, Uruk-hai have flooded through the walls and the defenders of the fortress have been pushed back to the throne room. Yet even as hope is fading for those that remain within Helm’s Deep, help is not far away – for dawn is about to break on the fifth day… Atop the hills that surround the Deeping-coomb, the valley that contains Helm’s Deep, as the morning light begins to crest the hills, Gandalf can be seen riding Shadowfax – and he has brought help with him. Having found Éomer and the rest of the exiled Rohirrim, Gandalf has led them with haste to defend the Hornburg from the amassed armies of the White Hand and, after riding through day and night, they have reached the battle just in time. RIDERS OF ÉOMER The Marshal of the Riddermark rides with his Éored and other loyal Rohirrim who stood by Éomer when he was cast out under the orders of Gríma Wormtongue. Each of these riders is a warrior of great skill and prowess, trained in the art of warfare from horseback for many years, and have gained great experience fighting under the guidance of Éomer. Under the command of their Marshal, these riders have come to liberate their kin besieged within Helm’s Deep, and will give their all to ensure they do. With a rousing shout of ‘To the King!’ from Éomer, the Rohirrim begin the rapid descent down the hill and towards the ranks of Uruk-hai below. The timing of their arrival was well prepared by Gandalf, for as they charge towards the fray the morning sunlight bursts over the peaks of the hills behind them, blinding the Uruk-hai and rendering them all but helpless against the ferocity of the Rohan charge.

content: RIDERS OF THÉODEN RIDERS OF THÉODEN A s the Battle of Pelennor Fields rages on, things are looking increasingly bleak for the city of Minas Tirith – its gates have been breached, its walls scaled and now hordes of Orcs have begun to flood the lower levels. Yet as dawn breaks over the Pelennor, from the north the sound of horns can be heard ringing out across the crisp morning air, heralding the arrival of the Riders of Théoden. As the sun rises over the Pelennor, and the Orcs seek to press the advantage, thousands of Riders of Rohan come into view from over the hills to the north, their spears gleaming in the morning sun. At the head of the army is King Théoden, clad in his royal armour. With his men behind him and the hordes of Mordor before him, Théoden gives a rousing speech for the ages, one that will stir the hearts of all who ride with him to untold acts of courage and turn even the most craven hearted into steadfast and resolute warriors. With a series of war cries, the king leads the charge headlong towards the fray. At his side are his most trusted marshals and captains: his nephew Éomer, a mighty warrior in his prime, Gamling, the head of his Royal Guard who carries the colours of the king aloft, and, unbeknownst to Théoden, Éowyn rides into battle disguised as one of his riders, carrying the Hobbit Merry with her as she does so. Each of these will fight to the death for their king and will all achieve acts of great heroism in the battle to come. When the Riders of Théoden charge into battle, there are few who can stand against their fearsome charge – its full force is enough to smash aside shield walls, trample their enemies underfoot and scatter those who have the sense to flee. The sight of such an awesome charge is enough to rally any ally to their cause with renewed hope and rout those who stand against them.

book: Armies of the Lord of the Rings
content: ARMY OF EDORAS D uring the reign of Helm Hammerhand, the kingdom of Rohan is at relative peace. The revolts of the Hill Tribes have been quashed, and Orc raids have become few and far between. Yet the standing armies of Rohan remain well trained and ready for war – for peace is a delicate thing and it doesn’t take much for it to shatter under the right circumstances – something Helm discovers following the death of Freca and the war his son, Wulf, brings upon Rohan. Helm leads the armies of Rohan in defence of its capital of Edoras. A strong and noble warrior and a veteran of many battles, Helm leads his army from the front. At his side ride his two sons, Haleth and Háma, both capable fighters trained in the art of war and skilled with both blade and bow. The sight of the king and his heirs striding into the thick of the fighting without fear is a sight that inspires their warriors to steel themselves against any foe. ARMY OF EDORAS The enormity of Wulf’s army requires that every able-bodied Rohirrim must fight for the defence of Edoras. With the city ablaze around her, Helm’s daughter, Héra, takes up her blade alongside Olwyn, an ageing Shieldmaiden, and Lief, an esquire of the king, each of them stoically fending off the armies raised by Wulf as they give their all to defend Helm’s kingdom from ruin. The armies of Edoras are made up of the best warriors the kingdom of Rohan has to offer. Their warriors are hardy folk who have pledged themselves to fight for their liege and his royal line against any foe that would threaten to raze their homeland to the ground. Should Helm or his heirs call for the Rohirrim to redouble their efforts, then the warriors and riders of Rohan will fight with every ounce of strength and fury they can muster, without a moment’s hesitation; and it would take an army at least twice their size to hope to overcome them.

book: Armies of the Lord of the Rings
content: DEFENDERS OF THE HORNBURG E doras has fallen, the king’s sons have been slain and the few Rohirrim who survive have been driven back to the fortress of the Hornburg where they are besieged by Wulf’s vast army of Dunlendings and Hill Tribesmen. The loss of his sons has driven Helm Hammerhand mad with grief, becoming a dishevelled wreck muttering under his breath, no longer fit to rule over his subjects as he once had; a state that sees the king seemingly disappear from the fortress itself. With her father no longer capable of ruling, it is his daughter, Héra, who takes up command of the armies of the Hornburg. With her allies Olwyn and Lief at her side to provide her with counsel, Héra rallies those within the fortress to prepare for war. For though she may not be the king, the blood of Helm Hammerhand still runs through Héra’s veins, and she has been blessed to inherit his famous stoicism and natural ability to lead. DEFENDERS OF THE HORNBURG Those who defend the Hornburg against the rabble of Hill Tribesmen now camped outside their gates know that they are facing the greatest threat to Rohan’s existence in the kingdom’s history. Yet in the face of such impossible odds, the Rohirrim refuse to simply resign themselves to defeat. Instead, they steel themselves for the battles ahead and prepare to give their all for the defence of their kingdom, and to fight with every ounce of strength, courage and valour they can muster to avenge those cut down by Wulf’s armies. Yet even in the blighted winter landscape, the defenders of the Hornburg do not fight entirely alone. Within the blizzards outside the fortress, an unknown force has been slaughtering Wulf’s men at night, picking off those who stray from the camp. Though the armies of Wulf believe the so-called beast to be a fearsome wraith, the truth is that even in madness Helm Hammerhand is a fearsome warrior and his grief has led him to avenge his fallen kin by any means necessary.

book: Armies of the Lord of the Rings
content: MINAS TIRITH MINAS TIRITH B efore the War of the Ring and the return of Aragorn, the White City of Minas Tirith was ruled over by the stewards, noble Men who were tasked with leading the great realm following the fall of the line of kings, until such a time that her rightful heir returned. In the final years of the Third Age, this duty has fallen to Denethor, a Man of noble blood though one whose desire for power runs deep; so deep that he may well be unwilling to relinquish the rule of the city should its king return. Under the command of Lord Denethor, Minas Tirith’s armies have long held back the forces of Mordor, becoming the first line of defence between the shadowed lands and the free peoples of Middle-earth. Yet constant war has taken its toll on Minas Tirith; the armies of the White City have run thin with their blood being spilt in wars with Mordor. Such conflict has also had an impact upon the steward himself, with Denethor turning to one of the lost seeing stones for guidance; an act that begins to crack his mind. Though at constant war, the armies of Minas Tirith are still a mighty force to be reckoned with. Each of their warriors is an accomplished fighter, trained from a young age to wield a blade and fight in formation. Clad in gleaming silver plate and carrying thick tower shields, the warriors of the White City form a nigh-on impenetrable bastion against the armies of the Dark Lord, standing strong against the blades of the enemy whenever they are called upon to fight. Yet it is not just these warriors that make up the armies of Minas Tirith. The most elite fighters are called up to join the ranks of the Citadel Guard or even the Guard of the Fountain Court. The White City also boasts an impressive cavalry division, with each of their knights armed with finely- balanced and razor-sharp lances. Yet it is those that lead the city’s armies that set Gondor apart from other realms of Men; heroes such as Boromir and Faramir are amongst the greatest the race of Men have to offer in the fight against the Dark Lord.

book: Armies of the Lord of the Rings
content: GARRISON OF ITHILIEN GARRISON OF ITHILIEN A t the eastern edges of the realm of Gondor, and next to the land of Mordor, lies Ithilien. This once prosperous land has become deserted and overgrown since the fall of Minas Ithil into the hands of the dreaded Nazgûl. Yet these lands still belong to the kingdom of Gondor, and patrols of warriors are stationed there to keep an ever- watchful eye upon their borders, ensuring no evil may cross into Gondor. At the time of the War of The Ring, it is the Steward’s own son Faramir who commands the forces of Ithilien; his followers garrison the ruins of Osgiliath as a last line of defence against the armies of Mordor. Stout warriors from Minas Tirith, skilled rangers who have spent years in the wilderness and hardy Men who have seen many battles within the city of Osgiliath are all under the command of Faramir, and will fight alongside him in defence of Gondor to the last man. Along with his trusted advisors, Madril and Damrod, Faramir leads bands of rangers into the wild lands of Ithilien, scouting ahead and ever on watch for intruders that have made their way into Gondor against the orders of the Lord Denethor. Those that do seldom make it far, for Faramir and his rangers will lie in wait hiding within the bushes and trees to strike. The first thing intruders will know of the trap Faramir’s men have sprung is the hail of arrows that rains down upon them, causing them to scatter before being picked off by unseen hunters. Yet even as the Third Age draws to a close, the forces of Ithilien and Osgiliath remain under the constant threat of attack. The armies of Mordor cross into their lands in tremendous numbers, assaulting the ruined city of Osgiliath with all their might so as to conquer Gondor’s last great bastion against the Dark Lord.

content: RECLAMATION OF OSGILIATH RECLAMATION OF OSGILIATH T he city of Osgiliath was once the great capital of Gondor, a shining beacon of the glory of the Men of Númenor rebuilt in Middle-earth. However, over the years of the Third Age, Osgiliath has been the target of many assaults from the forces of Mordor, causing it to fall into ruin and decay, becoming a crumbling shell of its former grandeur. Even towards the end of the Third Age, Osgiliath finds itself home to Orc bands using it for naught more than an outpost. Refusing to let the former capital remain in Orcish hands, Denethor has commanded that the city of Osgiliath must be reclaimed for Gondor and entrusts this task to his eldest son, Boromir. Carrying the banner of Minas Tirith aloft, Boromir leads the warriors of the White City against the Orcs that have infested the city, inspiring his followers to great deeds of valour as they seek to free Osgiliath from Mordor’s grasp. Such is the fury that Boromir fights with that those that stand against him are swiftly cut down. At Boromir’s side stands Faramir, his younger brother. Though he is not held in the same high esteem by their father, Faramir is still a valiant and exceptional warrior in his own right. It is Faramir who leads the Rangers of Gondor in the fights against Mordor, using their exceptional skills in tracking and moving swiftly to navigate the ruined streets and strike when they can catch the Orc armies unawares. Individually, both Boromir and Faramir are capable fighters, though together they are almost unstoppable. Many of the Men who fight alongside the two brothers have joined them on many campaigns before, becoming knowledgeable in the battleplans and tactics employed by the two brothers, and allowing them to fight even more efficiently on the battlefield. Such is the loyalty that Boromir and Faramir inspire in those they lead into battle, that when they fight to liberate Osgiliath from Orcish hands they will do so with a grizzled determination; so long as the sons of the steward stand tall.

content: ATOP THE WALLS ATOP THE WALLS W ith the forces of Mordor gathered upon the Pelennor, the city of Minas Tirith has been besieged. With Denethor’s mind having descended into madness with the loss of his son, command of the city and her forces has fallen to Gandalf. From atop the walls of Minas Tirith the White Wizard now has the task of rallying the warriors of Minas Tirith once more and steeling their resolve. Yet all is not lost, Minas Tirith is still a nigh-on impenetrable fortress that has never yet been breached in its long history. Great war machines line the walls, providing the city with the means of fending off their attackers from afar. These imposing Battlecry Trebuchets are designed to launch huge chunks of rock and broken masonry towards their foes, blasting huge holes in the formations of Mordor and bringing down siege towers with a single hit. It is these war machines that Gandalf hopes can stave off the advancing Mordor forces for long enough for their allies to arrive. However, should the walls of the city be breached, the seven layers of the city each have huge gates, and should one level be overrun then those who survive can fall back to the next and the defence can begin anew. Within the city walls, the Men of Minas Tirith will fight with renewed vigour, creating formations within the narrower streets to force the Orc armies away from vital areas and fighting all the harder to protect the people who make their home in the White City. Though command of Minas Tirith’s armies has fallen to Gandalf, he is not the only hero to stand at the defence of the city. The Citadel Guard have joined the White Wizard in the defence, fulfilling their duty to protect it with their lives should the need arise. At their head is Irolas, the Captain of the Guard, who commands his troops with an unwavering sense of determination and courage, even in the face of such fearsome odds. Even Peregrin Took takes up arms, standing true to his oath sworn to the steward and fighting with all the strength he can muster in the defence of the White City.

content: RETURN OF THE KING RETURN OF THE KING W ith the battle for the White City on the horizon, Gondor is short of allies. Though the Rohirrim ride south to war, their arrival may not be enough to break the armies of Mordor; they need more men. It is upon making camp in Dunharrow that Aragorn is met by Lord Elrond and presented with a unique gift: the shards of Narsil reforged into a new blade – Andúril, Flame of the West. Yet this gift also comes with a task; to travel the Dimholt Road and confront those who dwell in the mountain. For those who still inhabit the mountain halls are the spirits of those long since dead, those who promised to aid Isildur against the armies of the Dark Lord millennia ago, yet broke their oath and were cursed to rot and linger onwards. Upon reaching the depths of Dunharrow, Aragorn confronts the King of the Dead and uses the reforged sword of the King of Gondor to hold the dead to their oath, gaining their allegiance for the battles to come. When the Corsair ships pull into the docks of Harlond, it is not an army of Corsairs that leaps off the boats but instead a single Man, Elf and Dwarf. As the Orcs scoff at the three foes that stand before them, Aragorn summons the Army of the Dead to come forth, unleashing them upon the Orcs that stand before them catching them completely unawares. The sight of such a terrifying foe freezes the very hearts of the Orcish ranks, allowing the Dead to cut them down where they stand. Upon the fields of the Pelennor, Aragorn unleashes the deadliest army in all of Middle-earth. The shadowed legions sweep across the Pelennor, slaying droves of Orcs, Haradrim and Mûmakil, and they will not cease their ghostly assault until they have made safe the city of Minas Tirith from the armies of the Dark Lord. Such an act will serve to finally honour what the King of the Dead swore to Isildur all those centuries ago, allowing Aragorn to hold their oath fulfilled and allow them to be at peace.

content: DEFENDERS OF THE PELENNOR DEFENDERS OF THE PELENNOR T he Dark Lord Sauron has amassed his armies in Mordor, gathering to his side thousands upon thousands of Orcs and evil Men, and is now ready to unleash his full might upon the lands that oppose him. His hammer blow shall fall swiftly and impact hardest against the kingdom of Gondor; it is upon the fields of the Pelennor where much of the future of Middle-earth will be decided, for good or ill. Within Minas Tirith, the forces of Gondor prepare themselves for a war unlike any they have ever seen before. Every able- bodied warrior is called out to fight, though they are far outnumbered by the forces of Mordor that have amassed on the fields outside their gates. Led by the White Wizard, the armies of Minas Tirith are now faced with the greatest army of the Third Age – yet they do not face this threat alone… From the north arrives the Riders of Rohan, led by King Théoden who has come to honour the alliance that once stood between the two kingdoms. And from the south, Aragorn has arrived with his companions, Legolas and Gimli, and perhaps the deadliest army in all of Middle-earth in the spectral form of the Army of the Dead. Even with the lower levels of Minas Tirith overrun with Orcs, the arrival of their allies sees the turning of their fortunes in the war with Mordor. Together Men of Gondor, Rohan, and those long since dead fight to drive back the armies of Mordor and to ensure that the White City does not fall. Though the lives of many will be claimed in the city’s defence, those who do fall will be remembered as heroes who fought in the greatest battle of the Third Age, and stood up for what is right in the face of a dreadful and unrelenting darkness. ADDITIONAL RULES Rohan Warrior models can only be included in the Warband of a Rohan Hero. Gondor Warrior models can only be included in the Warband of a Gondor Hero or Gandalf the White. Dunharrow Warrior models can only be included in the Warband of a Dunharrow Hero, or in the Warband of Aragorn, Legolas or Gimli. SPECIAL RULES Defend the White City – Those that fought at the Pelennor have but a single goal – to ensure the White City does not fall. Each Hero in your Army can, once per game, declare a Heroic Combat for free.

Armies of the Lord of the Rings
content: MEN OF THE WEST MEN OF THE WEST T hough the Battle of Pelennor Fields has been won, the free peoples of Middle-earth do not have the time to celebrate their victory. Though the forces of Mordor have been driven back, the Dark Lord has not yet been defeated and behind the Black Gate he begins to amass his forces once more for an even greater attack upon Gondor. In doing so, Sauron has unwittingly placed thousands of Orcs between Frodo and the fire of Mount Doom. Within Minas Tirith, the leaders of the armies of the free peoples gather to discuss their options, and a plan is devised. They hope that by marching on the Black Gate they can draw out the armies of the Dark Lord, thereby emptying the lands of Mordor of Orcs. Such an act will likely result in the Men of the West all but forfeiting their own lives, but in doing so they will be able to provide Frodo with safe passage across the plains of Gorgoroth and one final chance to destroy the One Ring and end the power of the Dark Lord. Gathering their remaining strength, Aragorn and Éomer marshal their forces and march upon the Black Gate. Warriors of Minas Tirith and Rohan now stand side-by-side with one another against seemingly insurmountable odds as hordes of Mordor Orcs pour from the Black Gate. With little choice but to give their all and fight, the Men of the West will sell their lives dearly to enact the plan of their lords; it is only by the courage of Men that the day can be won. Yet the armies of Men do not stand alone, alongside them stands Aragorn’s allies and friends. Legolas and Gimli have endured beside Aragorn since the formation of the Fellowship in Rivendell, and Gandalf has returned to Middle-earth to help guide those who would see Sauron fall. Even Merry and Pippin have pledged their swords to the fight ahead. Together, Men, Elves, Dwarves, Wizards and even Hobbits will stand together in one final fight; the result of which will determine the very fate of Middle-earth – for good or evil…

book: Armies of the Lord of the Rings
content: NÚMENOR NÚMENOR A lthough they were exiles following the drowning of their homeland at the end of the Second Age, the coming of the Men of Númenor to Middle-earth would change its fate forever. Founding the great kingdoms of Gondor and Arnor to replicate the glory and splendour of their former home, the Men of Númenor soon became a dominant force, fighting back the armies of the Dark Lord and becoming perhaps the greatest and most powerful kingdom within Middle-earth. On the throne of Gondor and Arnor sat the High King, Elendil. Wise, noble and just, Elendil was a king beloved by his people and ruled in a manner befitting that of the great Númenórean kings of old. It was Elendil’s desire to see his new kingdom emulate the greatness of Númenor, a legacy that would be carried down by his son, Isildur, and by their descendants that shaped the kingdoms of Gondor and Arnor for centuries to come. The sable-clad armies of Númenor quickly became a strong martial power. In their early years in Middle-earth, the forces of Númenor faced evil warlords that ruled the lands, driving the cruel Haradrim back to the southlands, and besting the fanatical Easterlings that sought to invade from the east – yet they prevailed in every instance, proving that their valorous deeds and Númenórean steel could win out over the cruelty and ruthlessness of lesser Men. However, these wouldn’t be the greatest threat to Elendil and his people… When the hammer of Sauron fell upon Middle-earth, it was Gondor and Arnor that felt his wrath the hardest. Bands of Orcs raided the borders of Elendil’s lands, seeking to weaken the Men of Númenor and strike a sense of hopelessness into them. Such was the might of the forces of Mordor that even the armies of Númenor couldn’t face them alone, and so Elendil would have to form an alliance if his kingdom was to survive – one that would shape the future of Middle-earth.
